item.title: Gold pares intraday losses, keeps the red as bulls seem hesitant amid modest USD strength
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trims a part of heavy intraday losses to the $5,100 neighborhood, though it seems vulnerable following the parabolic rise of more than 25% since the start of this month and a series of record highs set over the past two weeks or so.

item.title: NZD/USD trades around 0.6050 after pulling back from six-month highs
item.description: NZD/USD halts its winning streak that began on January 16, trading around 0.6050 during the Asian hours on Friday. The pair remains subdued following the ANZ – Roy Morgan Consumer Confidence, which climbed to 107.2 in January from 101.5 in December, marking its highest level since August 2021.

item.title: USD/CHF rebounds above 0.7650 as traders brace for Trump's Fed nomination
item.description: The USD/CHF pair rebounds to near 0.7685 during the early European session on Friday, bolstered by renewed US Dollar (USD) demand. US President Donald Trump and Senate Democrats struck a deal to avoid a US government shutdown, supporting the Greenback against the Swiss Franc (CHF).

item.title: EUR/USD: Potential for further strength – UOB Group
item.description: UOB Group analysts Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann suggest that EUR/USD could see further strength, potentially reaching 1.2150. The report indicates that as long as the strong support level at 1.1890 holds, the upward momentum remains intact.

item.title: USD/INR steadies as RBI intervention looms
item.description: USD/INR rebounded after modest losses in the previous session, driven by weak Asian risk sentiment and flow pressures. Traders note the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) remains a key backstop against a move beyond the psychological 92.00 level.

item.title: Stocks: Mixed performance amid tech weakness – HSBC
item.description: US stocks mostly fell on Thursday, driven by losses in tech shares as investor concerns over AI capital expenditures resurfaced. European and Asian stock markets traded mixed, notes HSBC.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Tests 0.7000 support as 14-day RSI suggests overbought conditions
item.description: AUD/USD depreciates after three days of gains, trading around 0.7000 during the early European hours on Friday. Daily chart analysis indicates that the pair is remaining within the ascending channel pattern, indicating a persistent bullish bias.
